newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVE MARK CENTENARY WITH PLATINI AND ZEBRAS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVE MARK CENTENARY WITH PLATINI AND ZEBRAS.

text.p: Michel Platini, Paolo Rossi, 48 models in black and white dinner dress and two enormous zebra jigsaws helped Juventus celebrate their 100th anniversary on Wednesday.
Italy's most successful club side marked their first century of existence by bringing together dozens of former players for a festival of nostalgia at their gigantic Delle Alpe stadium.
Italy's hero from the 1982 World Cup Rossi was there, as were compatriots Claudio Gentile and Gianpiero Boniperti.
Polish striker Zbigniew Boniek and Irish midfielder Liam Brady returned to Turin alongside ex-Welsh international John Charles, now aged 65, who played for Juve in the late 1950s.

All were cheered as they marched around the stadium carrying a huge centenary flag, but the warmest welcome of all was reserved for former French captain Platini, arguably Juve's most successful player.

Platini, who scored 104 goals in 234 appearances for the club between 1982 and 1987, was mobbed by reporters and photographers and had to be rescued from adoring fans who managed to open a perimeter gate and storm the pitch.

After the parade, two wooden zebras, sporting the black and white stripes which Juventus adopted from English side Notts County early this century, were assembled on the turf by hordes of children in black and white T-shirts and shorts.
Television screens at each end of the ground showed slow motion black-and-white film clips of the greatest moments from an enviable soccer history.
Juventus were formed by Turin students in 1897 and actually date their foundation to November 1 of that year.
They plan to celebrate their true 100th birthday this November but decided also to celebrate on Wednesday with an out-of-season event at which they presented their squad for the 1997-98 campaign.
Forty-eight fashion models paraded in pairs across the pitch dressed in Juve colours -- the women in flowing white gowns, the men in formal dinner suits.
Each pair carried a little shield, or "scudetto", to represent the 24 Italian league titles Juventus have won.
Then came the football, as Boniek and Platini teamed up again to take on a team led by Rossi.
Some 15 minutes into the match, Boniek was brought down in the penalty area after a lightning run from midfield and Platini scored from the subsequent spot kick. It could almost have been 1983 again.
A bus carrying the squad for next season then drove into the stadium, where it was greeted by a firework display.
The current Juventus side, defending Italian champions, were introduced one by one to the 10,000 or so fans present before a second firework display brought the event to a close.
Juve's next centenary celebration is a friendly against English side Newcastle on August 3.
